findings.issue: A constrained fit record that is unreadable, not hash-complete, or missing `status` / `deployed.feasible` on one seed makes fit_feasible return False. The arm is then counted as CONSTRAINED_FIT_INFEASIBLE, which is a selection outcome, when it should be a technical failure. Claim B or C becomes NOT_ESTABLISHED_NO_ELIGIBLE_NOMINEE instead of INCOMPLETE_OR_INVALID. This breaks prompt sec. 10 ('fallbacks distinguishing ... technical failures'), sec. 12 statuses, and the module docstring ('A missing / nonfinite field ... is a TECHNICAL failure ... never a shortfall'). Reachability is limited, hence RECOMMENDED rather than REQUIRED: a missing fit unit directory already fails earlier as technical in release_hash, and the registered mapper always writes both keys. The misclassification needs a fit unit whose record.json is unreadable, half-written or schema-drifted while its release.npz still loads; fit_feasible never checks R.done(unit).
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: fit_feasible caught every exception and returned False, and a record without status / deployed.feasible returned False, so a technical record defect became CONSTRAINED_FIT_INFEASIBLE (lcr/select.py 114-127 = lra port lines 115-128)
findings.resolution: fit_feasible returns (True | False | None, detail). None (TECHNICAL) for a fit unit that is missing or not hash-complete, an unreadable record, a status outside {FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE}, a missing or non-boolean deployed.feasible, a record naming another configuration / seed, or a status that disagrees with deployed.feasible (FEASIBLE with False or INFEASIBLE with True; the registered mapper never writes either); candidate_rows turns None into the technical reason FIT_RECORD_TECHNICAL_FAILURE (registered in lra.family.SELECTION_REASONS / TECHNICAL_SELECTION_REASONS, LABEL_TRUTH_TABLE.json, SELECTION_RULES.json), the row is not ok and every role whose pool contains it is INVALID_* with fallback_class TECHNICAL. Only a complete, consistent INFEASIBLE record (status INFEASIBLE with deployed.feasible False) is the scientific CONSTRAINED_FIT_INFEASIBLE. A technically invalid role blocks the evaluation lock (F13). A release unit that is missing is FIT_OR_ADMISSION_FAILURE first

findings.issue: alias_set picks simplest_family and simplest_construction independently over the full alias set. The resulting '<family>; <construction>' can name a pairing that no alias deploys. family.overall_label puts this string verbatim into the headline label, against prompt sec. 12 ('name the actual family and whether it is an existing/calibrated/weighted/constrained construction'). This is new in lcr: cbp named the family only.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: alias_set took simplest_family and simplest_construction as two independent minima over the alias set (lcr/select.py 275-288)
findings.resolution: consolidated with F09 into ONE representative rule (lra.select.alias_set / winning_name): one real member of the exact alias set, drawn from the role's own pick pool (P*: the privacy-trained codes), ranked by construction (existing < calibrated < task-only < weighted < constrained), family (LOCAL < SEQ-12 = SEQ-21 < JOINT = JOINT-SINGLE < JOINT-PAIR), configuration ID; the label names that member's own '<family>; <construction>' (never independent minima, never an '=' join); every alias is listed in aliases.full; decided_by_config_id_tiebreak is disclosed

findings.issue: This is a regression from the verified cbp/select.py, which reported `identical_to_untrained`; lcr drops that disclosure. K-LOCAL's only start is C-TASK, and W-LOCAL l0.01 starts from C-TASK too. Either one, with no accepted move, deploys exactly the privacy-untrained C-TASK release (or D1 FINE-TASK when C-TASK did not move). That release is then nominated as P* or N* and named 'LOCAL; constrained' or 'LOCAL; weighted', and nothing records that it is a privacy-untrained release. The ctask construction ranks 9, so it is never the name. This mirrors the sec. 10 rule that fixed-map D1 privacy maps must not be relabelled task-only: a task-only release must not pass as constrained search.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: lcr alias_set had no identical_to_untrained (a regression from cbp/select.py); a K-LOCAL that never moved from C-TASK would be named 'LOCAL; constrained' silently
findings.resolution: alias_set returns identical_to_untrained = sorted exact aliases whose truthful privacy_trained is False, for every role; P*, N*, J* carry it beside the role (statuses[x].identical_to_untrained, frozen in EVALUATION_LOCK); the P* name gets '; identical to privacy-untrained <ids>' and the B / C label components get '(N*|J* release identical to privacy-untrained <ids>; no privacy-training credit)' (lra.infer -> lra.family.overall_label disclosures); untrained aliases are never the named representative

findings.issue: When a required guard role has no valid nominee but some candidates are ordinarily eligible, pick returns INVALID with no config and no descriptive_config. This breaks prompt sec. 10 ('deterministic minimum-shortfall fallbacks, distinguishing ... missing comparator') and sec. 13 ('P*, N*, J*, T*, C*, C_pair*, Q or their prespecified fallbacks'; 'If a role does not exist, use only its fixed descriptive fallback'). eval_lock.scored_labels then drops P*, the useful-release candidate, from the locked scored list. The T*-guarded diagnostics best_d1_fixed_privacy and best_weighted_privacy lose their entries in the same way, which also removes the registered decoder-ablation pair. One technical failure among the 8 T* candidates (e.g. a missing REF|F0 inner unit) is enough. Claim statuses would not change: the role stays INVALID and the fallback is DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: pick's MISSING_GUARD_COMPARATOR branch returned no config and no descriptive_config, so eval_lock.scored_labels dropped P* (and the T*-guarded diagnostics) from the scored list (lcr/select.py 237-239)
findings.resolution: the branch keeps status INVALID_* (MISSING_GUARD_COMPARATOR; the claim stays INCOMPLETE_OR_INVALID) and adds descriptive_only, descriptive_config = the strongest eligible candidate by the ordering keys, fallback_rank_status INVALID_MISSING_GUARD_COMPARATOR and fallback_class MISSING_COMPARATOR; eval_lock.scored_labels therefore keeps P* and the best D1 / best weighted diagnostics (and their paired D0 versions); a missing guard comparator is a scientific outcome, not a technical failure, so the lock is still built

findings.issue: This is the requested check of run.parse_id privacy_trained over every id in run.scored_ids(). All 83 code ids are correct: the 24 D0, 24 D1 fixed-map privacy, 24 weighted and 5 constrained ids are True, and D0/D1 DIRECT-TASK and FINE-TASK, CLASS and C-TASK are False. The 5 continuous ids have no privacy_trained key in parse_id, so select.privacy_trained returns False for RAW-J, FARE and LEACE. selection.json and the public SELECTION.json therefore publish privacy_trained=false next to training='privacy-trained reference', which contradicts prompt sec. 10 ('RAW-J is privacy-trained'). The P* and C* pools are correct as registered (77 / 72 code arms), so no role changes. Claims review R-2 added the display field but left the false boolean in place.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: privacy_trained returned False for SRC|RAW-J_b0.3, REF|F and REF|E while training said 'privacy-trained reference'; the P*/C* pools were correct
findings.resolution: privacy_trained is truthful for every scored id (RAW-J, FARE, LEACE True; U and F0 False); pool membership uses the separate private_code (the 77 privacy-trained code arms: 24 D0, 24 D1 fixed-map, 24 weighted, 5 constrained); C* = 72 incumbents; the public SELECTION.json rows carry privacy_trained, private_code and training

findings.issue: A code release whose inner token_states is null (missing, or a nonfinite value turned to null by R._finite) is ordered as a continuous release (+inf states) instead of being a technical failure, contrary to the docstring. The risk is mitigated because lcr.audit.validate_all (inner_validation) checks token_states == alpha1 + alpha2, which feeds global technical validity.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: a null token_states on a code release became mean_states None and was ordered as continuous (+inf) (lcr/select.py 164-171, 193)
findings.resolution: a code release must carry a finite positive integer token_states, a continuous release null; anything else (null, 0, a fraction, a boolean on a code; any value on a continuous release) is NON_ESTIMABLE_INNER_METRIC (technical, the row is not ok); mean_states is None only for continuous releases (+inf for ordering only)

findings.issue: Role-level aliases compare resolved config IDs only. They ignore the exact release aliases (tokens AND probabilities) that select.alias_set computes for P*, N* and J*, so alias_of_by_role misses slot aliases between roles that deploy identical bytes under different IDs. Prose could then count one comparison twice, against LABEL_TRUTH_TABLE.role_level_aliases. No verdict changes.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: eval_lock.role_aliases compared resolved configuration IDs only (lcr/eval_lock.py 56-63)
findings.resolution: role aliases use actual release identity across all three seeds: select.role_aliases (and the independent re-derivation eval_lock.role_aliases(resolved, statuses), which must agree or the lock is refused) pairs two roles that resolve to one configuration OR to different configurations that are exact deployed-release aliases; release identity = sha256 of tok_i, q_i, hard_i on the permitted OSF_DEFENSE_FIT + AUDIT_FIT + INNER_SELECTION rows plus alpha_i (select.release_identity; assessment bytes never enter); alias_of_by_role flags the repeated slots

findings.issue: The P* label name '<family>; <construction>' takes the simplest family and the simplest construction as two independent minima over the alias set. The result can be a pairing that no alias member has. Privacy-untrained aliases (D1 DIRECT-TASK/FINE-TASK, C-TASK, D0 DIRECT-TASK) also count, so they can supply the construction word. The prompt requires naming 'the actual family and whether it is an existing/calibrated/weighted/constrained construction'. Its interpretation rule ('Decoder-only control wins -> withdraw the new optimizer contribution') depends on the construction word.

findings.source_location: role_aliases() line 56 / build() line ~127; lcr/select.py select_all alias loop line ~298
findings.issue: Role aliases, and therefore the per-slot alias_of_by_role, compare config IDs only. SELECTION_RULES.json defines exact aliases as identical DEPLOYED releases (sha256 of tok1/q1/tok2/q2), and the prompt says 'Deduplicate exact aliases but retain roles/slots'. When two roles resolve to different configs with the identical release on all seeds, the same comparison appears in two claims without being flagged. A reachable case: a K-JOINT arm returns its feasible source-JOINT witness unchanged. Its D1 release then equals U|JOINT|i8o64|l0.1|D1, and the config-ID tie-break ('U|J' < 'U|K') makes P* the D1 control while N* = J* = K-JOINT-PAIR. Slots P15-P22 and P26-P33 then repeat P04-P11 but are not marked. Alias sets are also computed only for P*, N* and J*, so comparator release aliases are invisible. Caveat: release_hash compares raw token IDs, so a release that differs only by canonical token relabelling is still missed.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: alias sets were computed only for P*, N*, J* (comparator release aliases invisible) and release_hash read every row including assessment rows
findings.resolution: DUPLICATE/EXTENSION of F07, consolidated: alias sets are computed for EVERY role (P*, N*, J*, T*, C*, C_pair*, Q) on its nominee or fallback; same-token / different-decoder releases are never full-release aliases; canonical first-occurrence token renamings are recorded separately as canonical_equivalent / role_canonical_equivalence (informational, never byte identity); hashes use permitted fitting/inner rows only

findings.source_location: __main__ (writes EVALUATION_LOCK regardless of technical_validity.ok); lcr/assess.py does not refuse on it
findings.issue: The lock is written, and the single assessment can be opened, even when technical_validity already shows a failed control, a failed or missing gate, failed inner validation or a missing admission. That result is INCOMPLETE_OR_INVALID by construction, so the one locked opening is spent on it. The prompt says a failed control triggers engineering review, and the controls run before the assessment.
findings.verified_against_pinned_code: CONFIRMED at the pin: eval_lock __main__ wrote the lock regardless of technical_validity.ok and lcr/assess.py did not refuse on it; the source patch added an --accept-technical-failure escape, which this study does NOT adopt
findings.resolution: the source patch's escape flag is rejected (prompt sec. 13 stage 5/18.13). lra.eval_lock.main refuses (no file written) unless technical_validity is ok: controls verdict all_ok, ENGINEERING_READY bound and on origin, CORRECTNESS_LOCK / SCIENCE_LOCK present and SCIENCE_LOCK verifying, inner validation ok, no selection technical failure (any candidate technical failure or technically INVALID role), admission ADMITTED; any extra argument (e.g. --accept-technical-failure) is refused with a usage error. lra.assess.open_assessment calls verify_validity(lock) before any unsealing: technical_validity.ok True, ENGINEERING_READY bound and still ready with the same sha256, CORRECTNESS/SCIENCE locks byte-identical to the lock's record, the locked control verdict unchanged and all_ok, admission ADMITTED; open_assessment has no parameter that skips it. Resolution of a failure = repair + a new pushed lock

findings.issue: The working tree now checks Q PASS before INCOMPLETE (family.overall_label, LABEL_TRUTH_TABLE.json and test_truth_table.py all agree). The PROTOCOL bullet 'Any incomplete work without a passing component: INCOMPLETE_OR_INVALID' does not say whether Q counts as a component, so the text can be read against the code.

findings.resolution: precedence explicit and identical in lra.family.overall_label, LABEL_TRUTH_TABLE.json overall_label_rules_in_precedence_order and PROTOCOL.md sec. 12: (1) pre-science blocker NOT RUN (ENGINEERING_BLOCKED_NOT_RUN, then INCOMPLETE_NOT_RUN with its reason); (2) global technical failure after science INCOMPLETE_OR_INVALID; (3) passing method components; (4) Q-only CONFIDENCE_FEASIBILITY_ESTABLISHED_NO_METHOD_CRITERION; (5) remaining incomplete work INCOMPLETE_OR_INVALID; (6) EXPERIMENTAL_NO_ADVANTAGE.
